payload.goal: An incremental, local, derived index over the WHOLE repo so cross-record questions stop costing O(history) or O(initiative count). Tiered: Tier 0 is a byte-sized hot file (open sessions + held files) making cross-initiative conflict detection O(1) on the shim path; Tier 1 materializes the record graph for structural retrieval — exact, explainable, every result citing the event id that produced it. Maintained by per-initiative cursors so cost is O(new events), never O(history). LOCAL and gitignored: derived state never merges, never syncs, and rebuilds from truth when absent, stale, or corrupt. Zero model calls — the record has recorded edges, so retrieval traverses facts instead of guessing similarity.

payload.because: The log is append-only and ulid-ordered, so any derivation over a PREFIX is permanently valid — an index never needs invalidation, only extension. That makes cost O(new events) instead of O(history), which is the only way a cross-record answer can ever ride a 100ms shim: at 300 initiatives the measured warm sweep alone was 18.9ms and at 1000 it was 64.1ms, both O(initiative count). A MONOLITHIC index was rejected because parsing megabytes to answer a byte-sized question just moves the cost; the hot tier must stay small enough that reading it is free, and richer structure belongs behind an explicit ask. COMMITTING the index was rejected because derived state that merges is a permanent conflict source and a staleness vector across machines — local-only removes both problems at zero cost, since anything derived can be rebuilt. EMBEDDINGS were rejected as the foundation: they need a model (breaking felt-cost D3's zero-API-calls invariant, its cost and privacy guarantees with it) AND they discard the thing that makes this record special — the edges are already recorded facts, so traversal returns exact results that can cite the event id that produced them, where similarity returns guesses that cannot. Auditable retrieval is also what the drift work needs; approximate retrieval would be a new hallucination surface, not a fix for one. node:sqlite was rejected for now because it needs Node >=22.5 against a stated floor of 18; revisit if Tier 1 outgrows flat files.
payload.chose: A TIERED, INCREMENTAL, LOCAL index. Tier 0 is a byte-sized hot file (open sessions and the files they hold) read on the shim path; Tier 1 materializes the record graph for structural retrieval and is read only when asked. Both are maintained by per-initiative cursors (last consumed event id), live under a gitignored .sofar/.index/, and are rebuilt from the logs whenever absent, stale, or unparseable.
payload.over: one monolithic index file, a committed/union-merged index, embeddings-based semantic retrieval, and node:sqlite
payload.rule: The index is derived, never truth: it lives gitignored under .sofar/.index/, is never committed or synced, and any absence, staleness, or corruption must fall back to reading the logs rather than returning a wrong answer.

tasks.title: core/index/store.ts: gitignored .sofar/.index/ with atomic writes, a schema-version stamp, and per-initiative cursors. Any version mismatch, parse failure, or missing file yields a cold start rather than a wrong answer.

core/index/tail.ts: read events AFTER a cursor without re-reading the log — byte-offset resume validated against the cursor's event id, falling back to a full scan whenever the offset does not corroborate
open.json: open sessions per initiative + the files they hold, updated incrementally. Bytes, not megabytes — O(1) read on the shim path.
Wire cross-initiative conflicts through Tier 0, unblocking cross-initiative-conflicts 2.2; re-measure the shim against speed T2's 100ms at 30/300/1000 initiatives
Materialize the record graph incrementally into the index (nodes/edges from core/adjacency), keyed for lookup rather than rebuilt per query

Retrieval API + `sofar find`: traverse from a seed (file, session, decision, initiative) with a hop budget; every result carries the event id that produced the edge — exact and explainable, zero inference
Lexical layer over decision/note prose (IDF-ranked terms, no model) so text questions resolve to seeds the traversal can expand
SPEC: index layout, cursor semantics, the derived-never-truth rule, retrieval contract
Equivalence proof: indexed answers byte-match the from-logs answers on every fixture, and a corrupted/stale/absent index still returns the right answer via fallback

payload.note: core/index-store.ts. The index directory ignores ITSELF (a .gitignore of `*` inside it), so the user's own .gitignore is never edited — a tool that edits that file eventually clobbers it. Every failure mode collapses to one signal, null = start cold: absent, unreadable, malformed, wrong version, wrong cursor shape. Writes are atomic and silent on failure, because a record that cannot cache is merely slower.

core/index-tail.ts, 14 tests green. The cursor stores the byte offset where its event's line STARTS, which makes the seek self-corroborating: the first line read back must carry that id or the reader falls back to a full read. Pinned adversarially — rewritten log at a plausible offset, shrunk log, corrupt lines, absent log — plus the equivalence that matters (25 chunked appends land exactly where one full read lands) and byte-accurate offsets through em dashes and non-ASCII prose.

payload.next_action: Phase 2.1: build Tier 0 (open.json — open sessions and the files they hold, maintained incrementally), then 2.2 wire cross-initiative conflicts through it and re-measure the shim at 30/300/1000 initiatives.
payload.summary: Opened record-index and landed Phase 1, the incremental core. index-store.ts: gitignored self-ignoring .sofar/.index/, version-stamped, every failure collapsing to cold start. index-tail.ts: reads only what a log grew by, with a self-corroborating cursor (offset points at its event's line START, so the first line read back must carry that id or it falls back to a full read). 14 new tests including the equivalence that carries the design — 25 chunked appends land exactly where one full read lands — plus rewritten/shrunk/corrupt-log fallbacks and byte-accurate offsets through non-ASCII prose. 1155 green. Architecture decision recorded with the rejections: monolithic index, committed index, embeddings, node:sqlite.
